Quick triage notes — I pulled the runtime logs and traces for Acme's tenant. Correlation looks strong with last night's rollout of model-v2.3-quantized (deployed 02/17 01:12 UTC). Observations: 

- Elevated 5xx errors map to backend process OOMs and kernel fallback warnings in the NVIDIA runtime. When the quantized variant hits certain sequence lengths, we see a slow fallback path that stalls requests for multiple seconds.
- 429s coincide with our upstream rate limiter rejecting requests while retry storms from clients amplify load.
- Request queueing + aggressive batching triggered longer service times for a subset of shards.

Short-term mitigation I can implement in the next 20–30m:
- Initiate rollback to model-v2.2 for Acme's traffic (immediate)
- Apply temporary per-tenant retry damping (increase base backoff, cap retries)
- Disable aggressive batching and revert quantization flags for Acme's deployment

I'm attaching a small runtime_log_excerpt.txt with the OOM and kernel warnings (cut). Will coordinate with Rishi on capacity changes if we need an emergency scale-up.

-- Dev

Redwood Inference

Adding more context from infra + runtime:

- Root cause (prelim): a quantization profile change plus a kernel selection edge-case introduced a regression in the GPU execution path for model-v2.3-quantized. For certain token-length distributions (which match Acme's requests), the runtime falls back to a slower codepath that holds CUDA streams longer than expected and increases tail latency.
- That tail latency caused gateway timeouts; clients retried and our tenant-level rate limiter returned 429s once queues filled. The retry storm exacerbated the effect.

Immediate plan (we're executing now):
1) Roll back Acme to model-v2.2 (Dev starting rollback) — ETA 12–15 minutes.
2) Add per-tenant rate-limiter headroom temporarily and enable an emergency circuit breaker to return 503 quickly for requests that would otherwise cause long blocking — reduces retry amplification.
3) Post-rollback: run targeted canary across 1% traffic with increased telemetry and disable the new quantization flag until we patch kernel selection.
4) If rollback doesn't stabilize within 30 minutes, we will provision additional dedicated capacity in us-west as an emergency scale-up.

Longer-term: RCA and a hotfix for kernel selection logic in the runtime (possible kernel dispatch table bug) + additional pre-rollout perf tests for quantized variants.

Rishi Malhotra

Subject: Post-incident summary and next steps — Acme model-v2.3 rollout regression

Post-incident summary (brief) — timeline + corrective actions: 

- 2026-02-17 01:12 UTC: Rollout of model-v2.3-quantized starts.
- 2026-02-17 07:50 PT: Customer-reported spikes in 5xx/429 and elevated latency.
- 2026-02-17 08:05 PT: Triage identifies kernel-selection fallback + slow codepath for quantized variant.
- 2026-02-17 08:30 PT: Rollback to model-v2.2 initiated. Error rates returned to baseline by ~08:50 PT after retry damping and disabling batching.

Root cause (prelim): a regression introduced by a quantization profile change combined with a kernel dispatch edge-case in the runtime that produced a slow fallback path for certain token-length distributions. This increased tail latency which triggered upstream timeouts and retry storms, cascading into rate-limiter 429s.

Planned follow-ups / owners: 
- Runtime hotfix: patch kernel selection dispatch (Owner: Dev) — target ship 2026-02-23
- Hardening: add pre-rollout perf tests for quantized variants across representative token-length distributions (Owner: Rishi)
- Deployment policy changes: require 24-hour canary + telemetry for quantized model rollouts; automatic traffic-throttle if tail latency >2s during canary (Owner: Stephanie)
- Customer remediation: propose goodwill credit and formal RCA doc for Acme (Owner: Evelyn)

I'll prepare a detailed RCA and a timeline for the hotfix. Good job triaging quickly — reflect these learnings into the rollout checklist.

Rishi Malhotra
